text:
Rachael: quick thought exercise: if we push more private endpoints into customer VPCs, how do we want to handle DNS (split-horizon) + endpoint authz? Need a clear owner model.
Tom: two obvious patterns: (A) delegate subdomain to us (Route53/PrivateZone delegation) or (B) leave DNS to customer and run a resolver proxy in their VPC. each has tradeoffs.
Ibrahim: delegation is simplest for us for service discovery and cert provisioning, but customers hate giving write access to zones. compliance teams will push back.
Sana: resolver-proxy keeps owner control but adds operational pieces: resolver cache, PTRs, and latency. also raises risks around DNSSEC/validation and cache poisoning.
Rachael: authz: endpoints must assert tenant identity. options: mTLS with tenant certificate issued by central CA, or a signed JWT exchanged during handshake. mTLS is stronger for network policies.
Tom: if we do delegation + central CA we can automate cert rollouts via ACME-like flow. but delegated zone quotas and cross-account IAM are annoying. need a minimal IAM playbook.
Ibrahim: for resolver-proxy, propose a small control-plane handshake: stub registers endpoints with central CP, central issues short-lived SVID (SPIFFE-style) that the endpoint presents to our relays. relays verify SVID before accepting calls. avoids messing with zone writes.
Sana: SPIFFE-style approach covers auth and rotation neatly. challenge: revocation during partition. if central deletes service, how fast can we revoke SVIDs? TTL + push revocation recommended.
Rachael: also think about DNS caching semantics: tenant may expect an allowlist of our relay IPs in their firewall. if we are using shared relays, we should publish a stable set of IPs or a Cert+SNI mapping so they can use hostnames instead.
Tom: for private endpoints we can publish an endpoint manifest: {hostname, expected-cert-fingerprint, ip-list}. customer can pin either hostname or fingerprint. that helps when IPs are ephemeral.
Ibrahim: failure modes to document: stale delegation records, resolver-proxy crash, SVID revocation race, and split-horizon mismatch causing traffic to leak to public internet. runbook must include clear test to validate local resolution and cert fingerprints.
Sana: compliance: for some customers we cannot generate certs on their behalf. add CSR-upload flow where customer supplies private key origin and we sign their CSR. design must support both auto and manual cert flows.
cp-bot: scheduled test: private-dns-delegation-sanity-2026-03-23 (ETA 20m) :satellite:
Rachael: next steps: Tom to draft DNS delegation + IAM minimal steps; Ibrahim to spec SVID flow and revocation; Sana to gather compliance requirements and CSR flow examples. I'll consolidate into mini-RFC and post here.
Tom: will include an appendix with sample Route53 IAM policy and delegations.
Ibrahim: will model SVID rotation latency under partition and propose push revocation window.
Sana: will collect 3 customer examples that require CSR-only flows.
Rachael: thanks all. keep comments short in thread, i'll ping when draft is up.
